experiments.title: Baseline successful booking
experiments.description: Three-provider bookings (hotel, flight, transport) with no injected failures, executed sequentially to establish baseline latency.

criteria.description: Every request completes
One CONFIRMED lock per item (3 per booking)
Payment captured for every booking
No compensation attempted
Every transaction reached a terminal state
No ACTIVE (provisional) lock outlives its transaction
ROLLED_BACK/FAILED transactions hold no CONFIRMED locks
No 5xx responses

experiments.title: First-provider failure
experiments.description: The first provider (hotel) rejects its reservation, so no provider holds anything to compensate.

criteria.description: Every transaction ends ROLLED_BACK
Exactly one failed reserve per transaction and no successful reserves
Nothing to compensate
Authorized payment voided
All 3 locks per transaction released
Every transaction reached a terminal state
No ACTIVE (provisional) lock outlives its transaction
ROLLED_BACK/FAILED transactions hold no CONFIRMED locks
No 5xx responses

experiments.title: Failure after multiple successful provider reservations
experiments.description: Hotel and flight reserve successfully, then transport fails (Phase 4 scenario A); the two earlier reservations are compensated in reverse order.

criteria.description: Every transaction ends ROLLED_BACK
Two successful compensations per transaction
Compensation success rate is 1
Payment never captured; authorization voided
No CONFIRMED locks remain
Every transaction reached a terminal state
No ACTIVE (provisional) lock outlives its transaction
ROLLED_BACK/FAILED transactions hold no CONFIRMED locks
No 5xx responses

experiments.title: Successful compensation after capture
experiments.description: All providers reserve and payment is captured, then the transport confirmation fails; every reservation is compensated and the captured payment refunded.

criteria.description: Every transaction ends ROLLED_BACK
All three reservations compensated per transaction
Compensation success rate is 1
Captured payment refunded
No CONFIRMED locks remain
Every transaction reached a terminal state
No ACTIVE (provisional) lock outlives its transaction
ROLLED_BACK/FAILED transactions hold no CONFIRMED locks
No 5xx responses

experiments.title: Compensation failure / ROLLBACK_FAILED
experiments.description: Transport reservation fails and one or two cancellations also fail (Phase 4 scenario E and a double-failure variant).

criteria.description: Every transaction ends ROLLBACK_FAILED
One failed and one successful compensation per transaction (single failure)
Two failed compensations per transaction (double failure)
Each failed compensation leaves exactly one unresolved CONFIRMED lock
Persisted advisory is MANUAL_OPERATOR_REVIEW for every transaction
Every transaction reached a terminal state
No ACTIVE (provisional) lock outlives its transaction
ROLLED_BACK/FAILED transactions hold no CONFIRMED locks
No 5xx responses

experiments.title: Payment authorization failure
experiments.description: The payment gateway declines authorization after resources are locked and before any provider is contacted.

criteria.description: Every transaction ends ROLLED_BACK
Authorization failure recorded for every transaction
No provider operation was attempted
All locks released
Every transaction reached a terminal state
No ACTIVE (provisional) lock outlives its transaction
ROLLED_BACK/FAILED transactions hold no CONFIRMED locks
No 5xx responses

experiments.title: Payment capture failure
experiments.description: All providers reserve, then payment capture fails; every reservation is compensated.

criteria.description: Every transaction ends ROLLED_BACK
Capture failure recorded; nothing captured
All three reservations compensated
No CONFIRMED locks remain
Every transaction reached a terminal state
No ACTIVE (provisional) lock outlives its transaction
ROLLED_BACK/FAILED transactions hold no CONFIRMED locks
No 5xx responses

findings: Payment reversal recorded after capture failure: {"REFUNDED":10} (the payment was never captured).

experiments.title: Duplicate idempotency requests (sequential)
experiments.description: Each key is sent several times with the same payload (successful and rolled-back originals), then once with a different payload.

criteria.description: Exactly one transaction per key (success and rollback originals)
All duplicates served as replays
Replayed responses identical to the original
Reused key with a different payload rejected (422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED)
Rejected mismatches created no transactions
Every transaction reached a terminal state
No ACTIVE (provisional) lock outlives its transaction
ROLLED_BACK/FAILED transactions hold no CONFIRMED locks
No 5xx responses

findings: 30 of 30 replayed responses were byte-identical to the original response.

experiments.title: Concurrent requests using the same idempotency key
experiments.description: For each concurrency level, groups of identical requests sharing one key are released simultaneously.

criteria.description: Exactly one transaction per key at every concurrency level
All other concurrent requests replayed
Every response in a group carries the same transactionId
No request gave up waiting (IDEMPOTENT_REQUEST_IN_PROGRESS)
Every transaction reached a terminal state
No ACTIVE (provisional) lock outlives its transaction
ROLLED_BACK/FAILED transactions hold no CONFIRMED locks
No 5xx responses

experiments.title: Concurrent attempts against the same inventory
experiments.description: N simultaneous single-flight bookings (distinct keys) compete for a flight with capacity C; the engine must never confirm more than C.

criteria.description: Exactly min(C, N) bookings complete
CONFIRMED locks never exceed capacity
The remainder is rejected at reservation
Exactly min(C, N) bookings complete
CONFIRMED locks never exceed capacity
The remainder is rejected at reservation
Every transaction reached a terminal state
No ACTIVE (provisional) lock outlives its transaction
ROLLED_BACK/FAILED transactions hold no CONFIRMED locks
No 5xx responses

experiments.title: Reservation-lock contention
experiments.description: Hot-row sweep: bookings on the same hotel+flight rows at increasing concurrency (capacity sufficient, so contention is on row locks). Plus opposite item orders to probe lock-ordering deadlocks.

criteria.description: Every contended booking completes (capacity is sufficient)
No request rejected under contention
No deadlock errors with opposite item orders
Every transaction reached a terminal state
No ACTIVE (provisional) lock outlives its transaction
ROLLED_BACK/FAILED transactions hold no CONFIRMED locks
No 5xx responses

findings: Measured throughput (req/s) per variant: hot-row-c1=14.61, hot-row-c2=9.34, hot-row-c4=5.58, hot-row-c8=9.16, hot-row-c16=7.46, opposite-order=8.21.

experiments.title: Multi-provider transactions with different failure points
experiments.description: Every provider count k = 1..4 crossed with every failure point (none, reserve@i, confirm@i, reserve@k+cancel@1).

criteria.description: Every cell ends in the state, compensations, payment and lock outcome the Saga defines
All failure-point cells executed
Saga latency measured for every provider count
Every transaction reached a terminal state
No ACTIVE (provisional) lock outlives its transaction
ROLLED_BACK/FAILED transactions hold no CONFIRMED locks
No 5xx responses

experiments.title: Risk assessment under different provider conditions
experiments.description: Deterministic telemetry conditions (applied to all 3 providers via riskOverrides), provider counts 1-4, and capacity pressure. Bookings still execute: risk is advisory.

criteria.description: Identical conditions always produce identical scores
Every booking still completes regardless of risk
The combined worst case scores at least as high as every other condition
Score does not decrease as provider count grows
Decision is REVIEW exactly when level is HIGH
Every transaction reached a terminal state
No ACTIVE (provisional) lock outlives its transaction
ROLLED_BACK/FAILED transactions hold no CONFIRMED locks
No 5xx responses

experiments.title: Recovery-advisor classification under different failure evidence
experiments.description: Real failed transactions with controlled error evidence and provider telemetry; the persisted advisory is recorded and the read-only advisor is also evaluated directly on the same persisted evidence.

transient-timeout.rule: transient error, active provider, no lock/compensation issue

criteria.description: Direct classification matches the advisor’s documented decision rules
Each condition classifies identically across trials
Saga persists advisories only for ROLLBACK_FAILED
Every transaction reached a terminal state
No ACTIVE (provisional) lock outlives its transaction
ROLLED_BACK/FAILED transactions hold no CONFIRMED locks
No 5xx responses

findings: Persisted advisories by final state: {"ROLLBACK_FAILED":6}. The saga invokes the advisor only on ROLLBACK_FAILED.

Direct evaluation on the same evidence produced: {"AUTOMATIC_RETRY":3,"ALTERNATIVE_PROVIDER":9,"MANUAL_OPERATOR_REVIEW":15}. AUTOMATIC_RETRY, ALTERNATIVE_PROVIDER were observed only through direct evaluation, never persisted by the saga.
